To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) DNA copy number alterations are highly frequent in mouse fibrosis‐ associated hepatocellular carcinoma; 2) the DNA copy number alterations in mouse fibrosis-associated hepatocellular carcinoma are concordant with DNA copy number alterations found in human fibrosis-associated hepatellular carcinoma; and 3) the mouse model of fibrosi-associated hepatocellular carinoma is useful in replicating the DNA copy number alteration patterns found in human fibrosi-associated hepatoellular carcinoma

(1) DNA copy number alterations are a common feature of fibrosis‐ associated hepatocellular carcinoma, (2) the DNA copy number alterations in the mouse liver tumors are highly concordant with the human liver tumors, and (3) these findings demonstrate the utility of the mouse model in studying the molecular features of hepatocellular carcinoma.

(i) DNA CNAs are a hallmark of fibrosis‐related hepatocarcinoma in both mice and humans; (ii) CNAs in mouse liver tumors are similar to those found in human HCC; (iii) the mouse model of fibrotic hepatocarcinogenis is a useful tool for the study of human HCC
